licenses.electedBecause: The grant is named in the dataset record and its articles sit in a separate instrument, and the two are reached from the service rather than from a search. `https://geo.api.vlaanderen.be/ad/wfs?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetCapabilities`, 131,001 bytes, sha256 `317c2e322dde870fe7c2c6d2f9dec05e486bac96ae1ccd398638f090110d028b`, states `<Fees>Het gebruik van de service is kosteloos.</Fees>`, which prices the service rather than licensing the data, and points `AccessConstraints` at a `gebruiksrecht` page whose own words send the reader onward: `Gelieve de toegangs- en gebruiksbepalingen te raadplegen in de metadata van alle datasets die in de service worden aangeboden`. Its per-type `MetadataURL` gives CSW record `5c52b299-8f05-4d35-9839-a42934f1e619`, retrieved at `https://metadata.vlaanderen.be/srv/dut/csw?request=GetRecordById&service=CSW&version=2.0.2&ElementSetName=full&id=5c52b299-8f05-4d35-9839-a42934f1e619&OUTPUTSCHEMA=http://www.isotc211.org/2005/gmd`, 57,258 bytes, sha256 `71c827ecab5e485be1900b975849417ab3f47242e96fc97608f9493ef3d861b2`, whose title reads `Adressen`. That record carries two `MD_LegalConstraints` blocks and the distinction matters. The access block states `Geen beperkingen op de publieke toegang.` against the INSPIRE codelist term `noLimitations`. The re-use block names four instruments: `Modellicentie voor gratis hergebruik` at `https://data.vlaanderen.be/id/licentie/modellicentie-gratis-hergebruik/v1.0`, two instruments for public-task use by GDI-Vlaanderen participants and by bodies that are not participants, and the attribution string `Bron: Digitaal Vlaanderen`. A re-user who is neither a participant nor a public body acting on a public task holds the first, and the two GDI instruments govern a use this repository does not make. The articles are at `https://www.vlaanderen.be/digitaal-vlaanderen/onze-oplossingen/open-data/voorwaarden-voor-het-hergebruik-van-overheidsinformatie/modellicentie-gratis-hergebruik`, 71,446 bytes, sha256 `c195c42c0b8578d784e779a012137bfdc4e44cb55f7fee0dd2b13a3db04d1f2b`. The identifier itself serves no text: it answers `text/html`, `text/turtle`, `application/ld+json` and `application/rdf+xml` with one 541,080-byte application rendering to its title, and `.ttl` appended to the same path serves the RDF, which states `cc:requires cc:Attribution` and `dct:type adms:licencetype/Attribution`. Article 3 grants a non-exclusive, worldwide right to re-use the product for any lawful purpose, `met inbegrip van het reproduceren, doorgeven, publiceren, aanpassen en commercieel exploiteren`. Article 4 makes attribution the only use condition and lets the licensor specify its form, which this licensor has: `Bron: Digitaal Vlaanderen`. Article 6 states that access, provision and re-use are free. Article 7 gives the licence indefinite duration. The instrument states its own compatibility with the Open Government Licence, the Licence Ouverte, CC BY 3.0 and ODC-By 1.0, and it carries no share-alike term. No SPDX identifier exists for it, so `spdx` is left out rather than approximating one, because `electedLicenseLabel` feeds the share-alike prefix filter.

fetch.because: Article 3 grants the right to reproduce and transmit the product, which is what paging the service performs, and article 6 states that access and provision are free.

extract.because: Article 3 grants adaptation (`aanpassen`) alongside reproduction, which covers reading the designator and the component references out of a feature. Article 2 defines intellectual property rights to include database rights, and article 3 grants re-use over the product rather than over a subset of those rights.

transform.because: Article 3 grants re-use for any lawful purpose including adaptation and commercial exploitation, so joining the four feature types into a token and tag corpus is granted. Article 4 adds one obligation that carries into the result: attribution as `Bron: Digitaal Vlaanderen`.

train.because: Article 3 grants re-use for `elk rechtmatig doeleinde`, which covers reproducing the rows into a training process and adapting them. Article 5 states that the licensee holds the intellectual property in the works it creates on the basis of the product, which addresses the resulting weights directly. Article 4 requires that the re-use comply with data-protection law, which this source's `personalDataReview` addresses.

redistribute-data.because: Article 3 grants publication and transmission. Article 4 conditions it on the attribution the licensor specified, `Bron: Digitaal Vlaanderen`, and provides the wording for a combined work where listing every source is impractical: `bevat overheidsinformatie, verkregen onder de modellicentie voor gratis hergebruik Vlaanderen v1.0`. Article 4 also forbids suggesting that the re-use carries the licensor's endorsement.

redistribute-model.because: This instrument answers the question CC BY leaves open. Article 5 states that the licensee retains all intellectual property rights in the works it creates on the basis of the product, `zonder evenwel afbreuk te doen aan de verplichtingen betreffende het hergebruik van het product in deze werken`. Trained weights are such a work, so they are the licensee's, and the product's attribution obligation carries into them.

commercial-sublicense.because: Article 3 grants a non-exclusive right to the licensee and states no sublicensing right, and article 5 reserves to the licensor every right the licence does not grant. Unlike CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(5)(A), this instrument makes no direct offer to a downstream recipient, so whether a recipient holds it by taking the product under the same standing public licence is a question the text does not answer. Article 7 also ends the licence of right on breach, which a sublicence would have to account for.

That clause governs the geoservices infrastructure, and this row records a file download rather than a service. The publisher's own page for the directory states that it is published `for use free of charge by everyone` and `can be used by the public administration, as well as by companies for commercial purposes`. **This election grants the terms and does not make the source ingest-eligible**: its `personalDataReview` reads `present`, which `ingestEligibilityProblems` refuses on its own.

transform.because: The same clause grants processing and commercial use, subject to the mandatory source reference.

train.because: Clause 2 grants use, reproduction and commercial exploitation of the data, which is what fitting a model on the rows performs. The source reference is owed on any resulting publication.

redistribute-data.because: Clause 2 grants distribution and making accessible, conditioned on attaching one of the specified source references, which for English is `Federal Office of Topography swisstopo`.

The download page itself, 47,023 bytes, sha256 `a70084b182fa4d978f1d92dddb059e9d7e625eb8e225ec56504c641e4c5ed82e`, states only that the file is free of charge. extract.because: Clause (1) permits the data to be `verändert, bearbeitet`, which covers reading the house-number, street, postcode and locality columns out of the file.

transform.because: Clause (1) permits merging the data with other data into new datasets, and clause (3) requires that changes be marked in the source note: `Veränderungen, Bearbeitungen, neue Gestaltungen oder sonstige Abwandlungen sind im Quellenvermerk mit dem Hinweis zu versehen, dass die Daten geändert wurden.`

train.because: `Jede Nutzung ist unter den Bedingungen dieser „Datenlizenz Deutschland – Namensnennung – Version 2.0“ zulässig`, commercial use included, and the only conditions are the source note in clause (2) and the change mark in clause (3).

licenses.refusedBecause: HM Land Registry licenses Price Paid Data in two parts, and the part this repository reads is the restricted one. The download page, `https://www.gov.uk/government/statistical-data-sets/price-paid-data-downloads`, 129,747 bytes, sha256 `1f3aab231a5a27359dd7ef94c39970eed918395626e7b9f267fafca2282f89f3`, states `Price Paid Data is released under the Open Government Licence (OGL)` with the attribution `Contains HM Land Registry data © Crown copyright and database right 2021. This data is licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.`, and then: `However, OGL does not cover the use of third party rights, which we are not authorised to license. Price Paid Data contains address data processed against Ordnance Survey’s AddressBase Premium product, which incorporates Royal Mail’s PAF® database (Address Data). Royal Mail and Ordnance Survey permit your use of Address Data in the Price Paid Data: for personal and/or non-commercial use; to display for the purpose of providing residential property price information services. If you want to use the Address Data in any other way, you must contact Royal Mail.` The same page defines the Address Data as `Postcode`, `PAON`, `SAON`, `Street`, `Locality`, `Town/City`, `District` and `County`. Those eight fields are every field this repository takes from the file: the house number, street, locality, county and postcode of a Great Britain address skeleton. OGL v3.0 itself, `https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/`, 10,450 bytes, sha256 `f5b2b9f2af63647cde889fa6c3508f5705925295b74912c68caa28dd37e64aa5`, excludes `third party rights the Information Provider is not authorised to license`. Training a general-purpose address parser, publishing rows that carry these fields, and shipping an index built from them are neither personal nor non-commercial use, and none of them displays residential property prices, so the OGL grant reaches the price, date and property-type columns and not the address. The route to permission is Royal Mail, at the `address.management@royalmail.com` address the page names. The guidance page `https://www.gov.uk/guidance/about-the-price-paid-data`, 130,925 bytes, sha256 `1ec6dda91071cf30490b6077e212bfc6938c330645d391a59c2ec24a54d6e704`, states that `Addresses used by HM Land Registry to describe land are mostly derived from Royal Mail address data`, which agrees. This is the reading MHCLG's energy performance notice gave for `gb-property-building-2`, from a second publisher whose address fields pass through the same AddressBase Premium match.

The Valuation Office Agency publishes the non-domestic rating lists under its own restricted terms and states that the Open Government Licence does not apply. Its download page, `https://voaratinglists.blob.core.windows.net/html/rlidata.htm`, 33,414 bytes, sha256 `dafa09c510cf68e3575adbdd256a7b95ff86f1193ecaeda5dce6bd355df49be0`, reads `VO Rating List Downloads are only available under our restricted` license terms and `open government licence does not apply`, and `The information must be used in line with the restricted license terms and conditions`. The row's note describes the lists as the commercial complement to Price Paid Data, which makes this the largest Great Britain business-premises register refused so far. The route to permission is the VOA's restricted license, whose clauses this reading did not open.

licenses.electedTerms: Open Government Licence v3.0
licenses.electedBecause: Ordnance Survey licenses four OS OpenData products, Code-Point Open, OS Open Names, OS Open Roads and OS Open USRN, under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Each download ships a `licence.txt`, and each one states `Your use of OS OpenData is subject to the terms at http://os.uk/opendata/licence` (Code-Point Open words it `Your use of data is subject to terms at www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/opendata/licence`). Both addresses redirected on 2026-10-14 to `https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/`, 10,450 bytes, sha256 `f5b2b9f2af63647cde889fa6c3508f5705925295b74912c68caa28dd37e64aa5`. OS's own `docs.os.uk` terms page, 2,936 bytes, sha256 `83e7e1047ff833d4144e451f596290543b5673915733d3a26b8d48cac5253d7e`, states that the OS OpenData terms `are contained within the Open Government Licence` and that the attribution statement `can be found in the licence file downloaded with the data`. The licence files read are Code-Point Open 2026-08, 346 bytes, sha256 `2273fa3818d2b009ab38c11f3cfc9563e48c0e9e940bf73c1a3685b3188255ad`; OS Open Names 2026-07, 438 bytes, sha256 `1be838dcdba14daa10f6a5015833100858711fcda9e495a9442c9295d357f99f`; OS Open Roads 2026-04, 190 bytes, sha256 `65f3f555aa3e42e93b4db24a29ad277beefd12bc4871076d558c1cc41a6b216d`; and OS Open USRN 2026-10, 442 bytes, sha256 `41e89b74974c31cbb39efec9d78db825107e8fca565611e7098f92c94c6be62e`. The attribution differs by product. Open Roads requires `Contains Ordnance Survey data © Crown copyright and database right 2026`. Code-Point Open and Open Names add `Contains Royal Mail data © Royal Mail copyright and database right 2026` and `Contains National Statistics data © Crown copyright and database right 2026`. Open USRN requires `Contains OS data © Crown Copyright and database rights 2026` and, `Where you use data relating to Scotland`, `This product contains data created and maintained by Scottish Local Government.` No licence file or page read restricts the Royal Mail-derived postcode data beyond that acknowledgement, which is a statement about the text read; the OGL's own exemption for `third party rights the Information Provider is not authorised to license` stays in force. Code-Point Open's `product-supply` page, 4,936 bytes, sha256 `3f71e7910ce3a0107af8217563eb8e193a715c37e91bb5166078fae8ebeb942a`, states `Code-Point Open covers postcodes for Great Britain`, and the 2026-08 release has no BT area, so no Northern Ireland postcode and no Land & Property Services term reaches these sources. This reading covers the licence only. A row that joins a real street to a real postcode and synthesizes a house number can reproduce a residential address, which is a question for the personal-data review in `source-resolutions.json`, not for this reading.

Each download ships a `licence.txt`, and each one states `Your use of OS OpenData is subject to the terms at http://os.uk/opendata/licence` (Code-Point Open words it `Your use of data is subject to terms at www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/opendata/licence`). Both addresses redirected on 2026-10-14 to `https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/`, 10,450 bytes, sha256 `f5b2b9f2af63647cde889fa6c3508f5705925295b74912c68caa28dd37e64aa5`. OS's own `docs.os.uk` terms page, 2,936 bytes, sha256 `83e7e1047ff833d4144e451f596290543b5673915733d3a26b8d48cac5253d7e`, states that the OS OpenData terms `are contained within the Open Government Licence` and that the attribution statement `can be found in the licence file downloaded with the data`. The licence files read are Code-Point Open 2026-08, 346 bytes, sha256 `2273fa3818d2b009ab38c11f3cfc9563e48c0e9e940bf73c1a3685b3188255ad`; OS Open Names 2026-07, 438 bytes, sha256 `1be838dcdba14daa10f6a5015833100858711fcda9e495a9442c9295d357f99f`; OS Open Roads 2026-04, 190 bytes, sha256 `65f3f555aa3e42e93b4db24a29ad277beefd12bc4871076d558c1cc41a6b216d`; and OS Open USRN 2026-10, 442 bytes, sha256 `41e89b74974c31cbb39efec9d78db825107e8fca565611e7098f92c94c6be62e`. The attribution differs by product. Open Roads requires `Contains Ordnance Survey data © Crown copyright and database right 2026`. Code-Point Open and Open Names add `Contains Royal Mail data © Royal Mail copyright and database right 2026` and `Contains National Statistics data © Crown copyright and database right 2026`. Open USRN requires `Contains OS data © Crown Copyright and database rights 2026` and, `Where you use data relating to Scotland`, `This product contains data created and maintained by Scottish Local Government.` No licence file or page read restricts the Royal Mail-derived postcode data beyond that acknowledgement, which is a statement about the text read; the OGL's own exemption for `third party rights the Information Provider is not authorised to license` stays in force. Code-Point Open's `product-supply` page, 4,936 bytes, sha256 `3f71e7910ce3a0107af8217563eb8e193a715c37e91bb5166078fae8ebeb942a`, states `Code-Point Open covers postcodes for Great Britain`, and the 2026-08 release has no BT area, so no Northern Ireland postcode and no Land & Property Services term reaches these sources. This reading covers the licence only. A row that joins a real street to a real postcode and synthesizes a house number can reproduce a residential address, which is a question for the personal-data review in `source-resolutions.json`, not for this reading.

fetch.because: OGL v3.0 grants the right to copy, publish, distribute and transmit the Information.

extract.because: OGL v3.0 grants the right to adapt the Information, which covers reading street names, postcodes and coordinates out of the published files.

transform.because: OGL v3.0 grants the right to adapt the Information, which covers joining postcodes to street centrelines and synthesizing a house number.

train.because: OGL v3.0 grants adaptation and commercial and non-commercial exploitation, and fitting a model adapts and exploits the Information.

redistribute-data.because: OGL v3.0 grants publication and distribution, conditioned on the per-product attribution statements in each download's `licence.txt`, including the Scottish Local Government acknowledgement for Open USRN data relating to Scotland.

redistribute-model.because: Whether trained weights carry the attribution condition is the question `internal/strategy/counsel-briefing-2026-09-27-part-2.md` records for attribution licenses, and the OGL text does not answer it.

commercial-sublicense.because: OGL v3.0 grants a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive license and states no sublicensing right. Whether that satisfies a commercial agreement is a drafting question.

licenses.refusedBecause: The General Pharmaceutical Council reserves commercial use in its web terms. `https://www.pharmacyregulation.org/web-terms-use`, 88,394 bytes, sha256 `c33632ff36e296d16919b1111b121206e59f261c0b6bad7a546f64e42b88983b`, states `You cannot use any of the content or material from or any part of our websites for commercial purposes without obtaining a licence to do so from either us or our licensors.` The registered premises list is published on that website, and this reading found no separate data license for it. A request to the council could produce one.

licenses.electedTerms: Open Government Licence v3.0, for every row outside Northern Ireland
licenses.electedBecause: ONS states one grant for its postcode products in two places that agree. Section 3 of the ONSPD user guide shipped in `ONSPD_FEB_2026.zip` (`User Guide/ONSPD User Guide Feb 2026.pdf`, 815,965 bytes, sha256 `11c5bff8d149f7bfe7e97e57a77a4e8374cf8c2ac4d197ae374442c7edca5b0c`) and the `Postcode products` section of `https://www.ons.gov.uk/methodology/geography/licences`, 35,242 bytes, sha256 `8bdf15d6572e48458a62ef5c0becf253138a6c02686f0b4265d22cc7576d365d`, read: `Our postcode products (derived from Code-Point® Open) are subject to the Open Government Licence. If you also use the Northern Ireland data (postcodes starting with “BT”), you need a separate licence for commercial use direct from Land and Property Services. We only issue a Northern Ireland End User Licence (for internal business use only) with the data.` and `You may re-use this information (not including logos or Northern Ireland data) free of charge in any format or medium, under the terms of the relevant data owners' licence. In addition, the following attribution statements must be acknowledged or displayed whenever the owners data is used: Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database right [year]; Contains Royal Mail data © Royal Mail copyright and database right [year]; Source: Office for National Statistics licensed under the Open Government Licence v.3.0`. The same page puts names-and-codes lookups under the Open Government Licence with the ONS statement. The portal item `3080229224424c9cb53c0b48f5a64d27`, 3,682 bytes, sha256 `b31f29cf4d2e2594cf884360be0fcff4c4d804927631cd366c7b044dc57af650`, links that page as its licence and states that the product contains Royal Mail, Gridlink, LPS (Northern Ireland), Ordnance Survey and ONS rights. OGL v3.0, 10,450 bytes, sha256 `f5b2b9f2af63647cde889fa6c3508f5705925295b74912c68caa28dd37e64aa5`, grants copying, adaptation and commercial exploitation on the attribution condition. Unlike HM Land Registry's Price Paid Data page, which licenses its address fields to Royal Mail and Ordnance Survey's own personal or non-commercial terms, this grant names no restriction on the Royal Mail or Ordnance Survey fields beyond the three statements, and the relevant owners' licence for Code-Point Open is the Open Government Licence (`ogl-uk-3.0-gb-ordnance-survey-opendata`). **Northern Ireland is outside the grant.** `BT` rows come only with the Land & Property Services Northern Ireland End User Licence, 103,424 bytes, sha256 `712db2b0416e9ce9f55c73087e7d73178a8ecd0f94cac1a97eed60a200669a96`, which is `personal to you` (1.2) and permits use `solely for your own internal business use` (2.1). What this repository read: the London ward names in `data/gazetteer/london-pairs-v2.jsonl`, taken from live postcodes in the eight London postal areas, filtered to `E09` local authority districts and joined by `wd25cd` to `Documents/WD Ward names and codes UK as at 05_25.csv` (237,008 bytes, sha256 `56e80079e97bb13b3a35f662990b0db77489b06460628110f1db142f569e67e9`). Every ward it names is an English `E05` ward, and no `BT` row contributes. The election does not reach a Northern Ireland row; reading one would need Land & Property Services' licence.

fetch.because: OGL v3.0 grants the right to `copy, publish, distribute and transmit the Information`, which covers downloading the archive. Northern Ireland rows arrive in the same archive under the End User Licence, which permits loading them on a system under the licensee's control for internal use.

extract.because: OGL v3.0 grants the right to `adapt the Information`, which covers reading the postcode, local authority district and ward columns and the ward-name lookup out of the files. The permission covers rows outside Northern Ireland.

transform.because: OGL v3.0 grants adaptation, which covers joining ward codes to ward names and writing (ward, London) pairs. The permission covers rows outside Northern Ireland.

train.because: OGL v3.0 grants the right to `exploit the Information commercially and non-commercially for example, by combining it with other Information, or by including it in your own product or application`, conditioned on the attribution statements. The permission covers rows outside Northern Ireland.

redistribute-data.because: OGL v3.0 grants publication and distribution, conditioned on the three statements ONS requires: `Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database right [year]`, `Contains Royal Mail data © Royal Mail copyright and database right [year]` and `Source: Office for National Statistics licensed under the Open Government Licence v.3.0`. `pair-index-gb.bin` and `london-pairs-v2.jsonl` carry ward names only, from English wards, and the en-gb model card and README print the statements. A Northern Ireland row may not be redistributed: the End User Licence is personal and internal.

redistribute-model.because: OGL v3.0 names inclusion `in your own product or application` among the permitted commercial uses, so shipping weights or an index built from rows outside Northern Ireland is permitted with the statements in the package's rights files.

commercial-sublicense.because: OGL v3.0 is a licence the Licensor grants to every user of the Information, worldwide and royalty-free, so a commercial recipient holds the same grant from ONS and no right needs sublicensing. The agreement passes on the three statements. It cannot cover a Northern Ireland row.

licenses.electedTerms: Who's On First data licence statement (link to https://whosonfirst.org/docs/licenses/ required; contributing sources credited)
licenses.electedBecause: The data repository's `LICENSE.md`, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whosonfirst/whosonfirst-data/master/LICENSE.md`, 725 bytes, sha256 `634276f100c598a3f8b79250a852383278857868a2d5efcf6639d485ae4a2cb0`, states: `Crediting Who's On First is recommended and linking back to the License is required. For example: > Data from Who's On First. [License](https://whosonfirst.org/docs/licenses/).`, then `The Who's On First dataset is both an original work and a modification of existing open data. Some of those open data projects do require attribution.`, and puts `The format and structure that allows Who's On First to operate` under a Creative Commons Zero designation. The licences page, `https://whosonfirst.org/docs/licenses/`, 48,404 bytes, sha256 `bb584e412810ef475b32264bf1d2b5c12f188006d5929b9441f56c2b5ddfc0ed`, repeats that text and lists 102 contributing sources, generated 2020-02-21. Its Great Britain and Northern Ireland entries are Ordnance Survey of Northern Ireland under the Open Government Licence v3.0, London Datastore under the Open Government Licence v2.0 (`ogl-v2.html`, 9,853 bytes, sha256 `f43b76732008f9cf9b51d6a8dc45db23289b784e79691e0de04cc08c51f6d9be`), GeoNames under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (`geonames-about.html`, 10,039 bytes, sha256 `5f2d1ce44aed6a4b7490e5381026ffe4228a2a19bdf4c08d2bb82ee4648bdc6f`), and Quattroshapes under CC BY 2.0 (`quattroshapes-LICENSE.md`, 3,962 bytes, sha256 `0cb7a0fed5e763159c9b43418381d722521d7c57d68b1bb87d9c26858eeb5887`), whose Great Britain input is Ordnance Survey with the statement `Contains Ordnance Survey data © Crown copyright and database right`. Each of those licences permits adaptation and commercial use with attribution, and none of them restricts the place names. The statement reserves nothing and names the link as its one required condition. It grants no licence of its own over Mapzen's original work beyond the format and structure, so this election reads the statement as permission conditioned on the link, together with the sources' own grants, and records the credits each source requires. What this repository reads: Great Britain and Northern Ireland place names, placetypes and parent ids from the admin database `admin-global-priority.db` (md5 `12a9d4b46242c18f6cd867f89208fdc3`), for the borough pairs in `pair-index-gb.bin`, `data/gazetteer/gb-regions-v1.jsonl`, `ni-pairs-v1.jsonl` and the neighbourhood rows of `london-pairs-v2.jsonl`. The database records a geometry source per record and no name source, so the credits cover the sources the page lists for Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

fetch.because: The project publishes the bundles for download and states the link as its one required condition. The contributing sources' licences (OGL v3.0, OGL v2.0, CC BY 4.0, CC BY 2.0) each grant copying.

extract.because: The statement describes the dataset as a modification of open data and reserves nothing. The contributing sources' licences grant adaptation, which covers reading place names, placetypes and parent ids out of the database.

transform.because: Joining a place to its parent and writing (child, parent) pairs adapts the records, which OGL v3.0 (`adapt the Information`), OGL v2.0, CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(1)(B) and CC BY 2.0 §3(b) grant on their attribution conditions.

train.because: None of the contributing licences restricts commercial use, and the Who's On First statement adds only the link. Using the pairs as a decode-time prior or as training rows is a use those grants cover with attribution.

redistribute-data.because: `pair-index-gb.bin` and the committed pair files redistribute place names and their parents. The statement requires the link `Data from Who's On First. License: https://whosonfirst.org/docs/licenses/`, and the contributing sources require their credits, including `Contains Ordnance Survey data © Crown copyright and database right` for the Ordnance Survey input. The en-gb model card prints the Who's On First credit.

redistribute-model.because: Every contributing licence permits including the data in a product, and the Who's On First statement requires only the link, which the weights packages' rights files carry.

commercial-sublicense.because: The statement grants no licence of its own that this repository could pass on, and the CC BY 4.0 and CC BY 2.0 sources are not sublicensable. Each grant is made to every recipient directly, so a commercial recipient takes the data on the link and credit conditions from Who's On First and its sources rather than from this repository.

licenses.electedTerms: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0
licenses.electedBecause: This is the same publisher, the same database and the same instrument as `unchecked-access-free-fr-institut-national-de-l-information-g-ographiq`, applied to ten jurisdictions that the register carries as their own ISO 3166-1 codes. That decision records the reading of IGN's conditions of use at `https://adresse.data.gouv.fr/cgu` and of the dataset's `license` `lov2` on `https://www.data.gouv.fr/api/1/datasets/base-adresse-nationale/`, and it stays the home of the reading for the whole-country extract it was made about. What this body adds is the evidence that the grant reaches these ten territories, which the metropolitan file alone does not show. **The Base Adresse Nationale publishes one gzipped CSV per INSEE department code beside the national extract, at the same path and under the same dataset record.** `https://adresse.data.gouv.fr/data/ban/adresses/latest/csv/` lists 107 department files, among them the three-digit codes 971, 972, 973, 974, 975, 976, 977, 978, 984, 986, 987, 988 and 989. Ten of those answer HTTP 200 with data and all ten carry the same 23-column header as the national file, read from each file rather than assumed: Guadeloupe 163,423 rows, Martinique 138,460, French Guiana 60,904, Réunion 340,941, Saint Pierre and Miquelon 3,049, Mayotte 52,588, Saint Barthélemy 5,553, Saint Martin 7,363, French Polynesia 7,713 and New Caledonia 51,702, which is 831,696 rows measured on 2026-10-01 with no ragged row in any file. `https://api-adresse.data.gouv.fr/search/` returns these as `type` `street` with `context` `987, Polynésie française` and `988, Nouvelle-Calédonie`, so the publisher treats them as part of the same address base rather than as a separate product. IGN's conditions state the institute's mission over `plus de 25 millions d'adresses sur le territoire français`, and the French territories are part of that territory, which is why no separate grant is needed for them. **French Polynesia needs one distinction kept.** The register separately refuses the Institut de la statistique de la Polynésie française, which reserves its rights over its own publications; that is a different publisher from IGN and says nothing about this file. Electing here does not disturb that refusal.

fetch.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 grants the right to reproduce, copy and publish the Information freely and for any purpose, which is what downloading one department's gzipped CSV performs.

extract.because: The same grant covers extracting and transforming the Information, which is reading `numero`, `nom_voie`, `code_postal` and `nom_commune` out of a row.

transform.because: The licence permits adapting, modifying and combining the Information with other information, which is what normalising a row into this repository's components does.

train.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 names no restriction on the purpose of reuse and attaches no share-alike term, so training a model on the Information falls inside `librement, pour tout usage`. The licence's one obligation is attribution of the source and the date of the last update, which the release artifacts carry.

licenses.electedTerms: Italian Open Data License 2.0
licenses.electedBecause: The ministry's catalogue page, `https://dati.istruzione.it/opendata/opendata/catalogo/elements1/?area=Scuole`, states `License:` with a link to `http://www.dati.gov.it/iodl/2.0/` on the entry for `DS0400SCUANAGRAFESTAT`, the register of state schools, and the fetched file `SCUANAGRAFESTAT20262720260901.csv` is that entry's 2026/27 distribution. The licence text at `https://www.dati.gov.it/content/italian-open-data-license-v20` grants a worldwide, free, perpetual, irrevocable licence to `estrarre e reimpiegare le Informazioni` and to `creare un Lavoro derivato`, defined as `ogni traduzione, adattamento, trasformazione, diversa disposizione ed ogni altra modifica delle Informazioni`, on condition of naming the source and the provider. IODL 2.0 carries no share-alike term. No SPDX identifier names IODL 2.0, so `spdx` is left out. The `it-miur-scuole` adapter trains on the rows; each row holds the school's address and never its name.

fetch.because: IODL 2.0 grants `riprodurre` and `estrarre e reimpiegare le Informazioni`, which retrieving the CSV performs.

extract.because: IODL 2.0 grants `estrarre e reimpiegare le Informazioni`, which reading the street line, postcode and comune performs.

transform.because: IODL 2.0 grants `creare un Lavoro derivato`, which it defines to include `adattamento, trasformazione`; rendering and labeling each address performs that.

train.because: IODL 2.0 grants `estrarre e reimpiegare le Informazioni` and `creare un Lavoro derivato`, defined as `ogni traduzione, adattamento, trasformazione, diversa disposizione ed ogni altra modifica delle Informazioni`. Fitting a model extracts and reuses the rows and produces such a transformation. IODL 2.0 carries no share-alike term, and its condition is naming the source and the provider, which the adapter's attribution states.

redistribute-data.because: No corpus built from the source is published; its rows stay on the data root.

redistribute-model.because: Whether trained weights are a `Lavoro derivato` of the rows is the question `internal/strategy/counsel-briefing-2026-09-27-part-2.md` records, and the licence text does not answer it.

commercial-sublicense.because: IODL 2.0 grants its rights to every user directly and names no sublicensing right, so there is no clause to read either way.

Its `ms:AD.Address` feature type carries a `MetadataURL` for CSW record `a3990e57-5f0f-4bd6-94c9-47d46b692087`, retrieved at `http://mapy.geoportal.gov.pl/wss/service/CSWINSP/guest/CSWStartup?request=GetRecordById&service=CSW&version=2.0.2&outputschema=http://www.isotc211.org/2005/gmd&elementsetname=full&Id=a3990e57-5f0f-4bd6-94c9-47d46b692087`, 26,698 bytes, sha256 `c2a86692a4adbcc08c0fe29e7046aab11f048788e7140994c793da2885d40f42`. That record states `title` `Adresy Addresses`, `organisationName` `Główny Urząd Geodezji i Kartografii (GUGiK) Head Office of Geodesy and Cartography`, `fileIdentifier` equal to the id the capabilities named, and `dateStamp` `2019-07-20`. Its `useConstraints` reads `inne ograniczenia`, the Polish rendering of the ISO code `otherRestrictions`, which means the statement sits in `otherConstraints`, and the two `otherConstraints` values read `Brak warunków dostępu i użytkowania` and `Brak ograniczeń w publicznym dostępie`: no conditions for access and use, and no limitations on public access. Those render INSPIRE's controlled values, as ČÚZK's `žádné podmínky neplatí` does in Czech and the Slovak Ministry's `Neuplatňujú sa žiadne podmienky` does in Slovak. No licence instrument is named, so no `spdx` and no `termsVersion` are written here and `electedTerms` records the publisher's own words, which is Czechia's treatment. The record ties to the measured service by its own `linkage`, which holds `https://mapy.geoportal.gov.pl/wss/service/INSPIRE/Addresses?REQUEST=GetCapabilities&SERVICE=WFS`, and its `code` values `AD`, `PRG.AD` and `http://iip.gugik.gov.pl/id/dataset/PL.PZGiK.200/PRG.AD` name the national dataset the theme derives from. One caution is recorded rather than smoothed over: the service's `inspire_dls:SpatialDataSetIdentifier` states the literal `mycode`, so the identifier that is meant to tie a download service to its dataset is an unreplaced placeholder here, and the per-feature-type `MetadataURL` is the tie that works.

fetch.because: The statement is that no conditions apply to access and use, so paging the service's GML is unreserved. The capabilities document agrees on price with `No fees`.

extract.because: A statement that no conditions apply reserves no act, so reading the locality, street, house number and postcode columns out of a feature is unreserved.

transform.because: No condition attaches to adaptation, so producing a token and tag corpus from the rows is unreserved. This payload needs no join across feature types, because each feature carries the whole address.

train.because: No condition attaches to any purpose, so fitting a model on the rows is unreserved.

redistribute-data.because: A statement that no conditions apply imposes no attribution condition. Crediting GUGiK stays good practice and the statement requires it nowhere.

redistribute-model.because: The question that stands open under CC BY and ODbL, whether trained weights are a derivative of the rows, does not arise where the publisher states that no conditions apply to use.

commercial-sublicense.because: A statement that no conditions apply leaves no right that would need sublicensing, and it is made to the public rather than to one recipient.

licenses.refusedBecause: MHCLG licenses the energy performance of buildings data in two parts, and the part this register needs is the restricted one. `https://get-energy-performance-data.communities.gov.uk/guidance/licensing-restrictions`, 19,402 bytes, sha256 `e2164d92b85e88b35db873985b278d02e0cc94576b70b9dca4ddb8ccf5682226`, states that `All data fields other than the address and postcode data` are under the Open Government Licence v3.0, UPRNs included. The address fields, address 1 to 3 and the postcode, were `processed against Ordnance Survey's Address Base Premium product, which incorporates Royal Mail's PAF® database`, and Ordnance Survey and Royal Mail `reserve all their respective copyright, database rights`. The notice permits the address data `solely for specific purposes related to the energy performance of buildings`, plus non-commercial research and private study, and states that `Any use of address data which is not specified in this notice … requires an appropriate licence from Ordnance Survey.` Training a general-purpose address parser and redistributing weights fitted on these strings fall outside the permitted purposes, so the route to permission is an Ordnance Survey license. The OGL fields alone carry a UPRN without an address string, which gives the corpus no labeled address text. The same service's `/guidance/data-protection-requirements`, 19,054 bytes, sha256 `599a56a0722221c25bdac7057bf9b6152b46c8971b0ee118c79782b0e41a6668`, states `Address level data concerning the energy performance of buildings constitute personal data`, which is a second, independent refusal under the 2026-09-30 decision that the corpus carries organization addresses only.

licenses.electedBecause: The Ministry states one condition of use and states it twice, in its own register and in that register's INSPIRE export. Reaching it took reading an error body rather than another search: the export URL the service's own capabilities document writes answers HTTP 422 with `{"loc":["path","collection_record_id"],"msg":"value is not a valid uuid"}`, which places the id in the PATH where the capabilities put it in the query, and a second 422 enumerates the permitted `export_format` values, among which `gmd` does not appear. `https://rpi.gov.sk/api/collection_record/86dea70e-a55b-4241-bd63-4024b3f76b72`, 9,335 bytes, sha256 `0937d4bffc3f3078e27aad12dc3649469969ec407a022da81125f2656ff6ff38`, is the record: `title` `INSPIRE - Adresy`, `unit_name` `Ministerstvo vnútra Slovenskej republiky`, `hierarchy_level` `dataset`, `status` `published`, `date_stamp` `2025-05-28`. It ties to the measured service by its own `downloadable_urls`, which holds exactly `https://rageo.minv.sk/geoserver/ad/wfs?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetCapabilities`, and its `spatial_scopes` reads the INSPIRE codelist term `national` with a `footprint_geo` of `Slovenská Republika` at a 100% match. Its `use_constraints` reads `Neuplatňujú sa žiadne podmienky (CC0 Voľné dielo)`. The same record exported as `export_format=inspire_xml`, 18,955 bytes, sha256 `710e0fc3216645b5c4014a4044dbaff86adc07da390b8a06b0e99055decdf28e`, carries `accessConstraints` and `useConstraints` both as `otherRestrictions`, the ISO code meaning that the statement is in `otherConstraints`, and two `otherConstraints` values: `Neuplatňujú sa žiadne podmienky (CC0 Voľné dielo)` and `Neuplatňujú sa žiadne podmienky`. That phrase renders INSPIRE's controlled value for no conditions applying to access and use, in Slovak, as ČÚZK's `žádné podmínky neplatí` does in Czech. The parenthetical adds the publisher's own identification of it as CC0. No version accompanies that label, so `spdx` and `termsVersion` are left out and `electedTerms` records the publisher's words, the same treatment Czechia's entry receives. The record also reads `is_opendata_allowed` and `is_hvd_compliant` true, so the Ministry publishes this as a high-value dataset under the Open Data Directive. The CC BY 4.0 an earlier pass recorded for Slovakia belongs to the geodesy authority's ATOM feed at `inspirews.skgeodesy.sk` and grants nothing over this service, which is a different publisher.

fetch.because: The statement is that no conditions apply to access and use, so paging the service's GeoJSON is unreserved. The capabilities document agrees on price with `<Fees>NONE</Fees>`.

extract.because: A statement that no conditions apply reserves no act, so reading the designator and the component references out of a feature is unreserved. CC0, which the publisher names, waives extraction and database rights explicitly.

transform.because: No condition attaches to adaptation, so joining the five feature types into a token and tag corpus is unreserved.

train.because: No condition attaches to any purpose, so fitting a model on the rows is unreserved.

redistribute-data.because: A statement that no conditions apply imposes no attribution condition, and CC0 imposes none either. Crediting the Ministry stays good practice and neither statement requires it.

redistribute-model.because: The question that stands open under CC BY and ODbL, whether trained weights are a derivative of the rows, does not arise where the publisher states that no conditions apply and names CC0, which waives the rights that would make the answer matter.

commercial-sublicense.because: A statement that no conditions apply leaves no right that would need sublicensing. CC0 §3 adds a fallback licence to exercise all those rights unconditionally where the waiver is ineffective in law, and it runs to the public rather than to one recipient.

The data.gov.au entry `geocoded-national-address-file-g-naf`, organisation `Department of Industry, Science and Resources (DISR)`, 14,325 bytes, sha256 `5ca0881b1fa1bb8d78d6a315a79b4f6e5b3db5267ee385dddac2e5cea2d01c4c`, carries `license_id` `cc-by-4.0`. However, an important restriction relating to the use of the open G-NAF for the sending of mail has been added.` The EULA resource, `20160226-eula-open-g-naf.pdf`, 235,236 bytes, sha256 `25d83084297928d5e1187e2aa8a31d6292db668405752208b0dc8bb275d3a95c`, grants in §2(a)(1) `a worldwide, royalty-free, non-sublicensable, non-exclusive, irrevocable licence` to `reproduce and Share the Licenced Material, in whole or in part` and to `produce, reproduce, and Share Adapted Material`. §2(a)(2) adds: `Use restriction. You must not use the Licensed Material for the generation of an address or a compilation of addresses for the sending of mail unless You have verified that each address to be used for the sending of mail is capable of receiving mail by reference to a secondary source of information other than the Licensed Material.` §3(a) carries CC BY 4.0's attribution conditions. The fact sheet, `fact-sheet-open-g-naf-use-restriction.pdf`, 85,389 bytes, sha256 `c80654fe35bb5b2a1ed95612fbbbf673918df199cfc20eedb24e2f29d7995174`, explains that the restriction `prohibits inappropriate use of the open G-NAF while permitting suitable use`. Parsing addresses and training a parser on G-NAF's address, street-locality and locality files does not generate an address or a list for sending mail, so the restriction does not bar this repository's use. It binds anyone who uses the Licensed Material itself for mailing, and it travels with any redistributed rows under §2(a)(6)(A). The current release on the entry is August 2026 (`g-naf_aug26_allstates_gda2020_psv_110.zip`). The EULA dated 26 February 2016 is the one the entry links, and it names no edition.

commercial-sublicense.because: The reuse right runs from the statute to `toute personne`, so a commercial licensee of the result holds it directly. L. 323-2 allows restrictions only through a licence, and ANS has established none for TRE_R35.

However, if you publish a produced work, the underlying database has to be published as well (or alternations to the original database as is the case of derived databases), according to section 4.6 of ODbL.` A parser's weights are not intended for extracting the original data, so they are a Produced Work, and the published extract meets 4.6. The extracts are read through Geofabrik, whose download page, `https://download.geofabrik.de/`, 9,609 bytes, sha256 `4b017225876c1edf6954a66da43dfb8104a7e7ecc93ca83f3d22c69eef59b570`, states `Data processed by Geofabrik GmbH and created by OpenStreetMap Contributors | License: ODbL 1.0`. The Substantial guideline, 44,919 bytes, sha256 `9a70503b9b062628cc63ddea60389dea9df9e51b0498551bf3d2b00289cf593f`, is retained. What this repository reads: address and name tags from Geofabrik extracts (`osm`, and the 2026-10-02 extracts for BD, CN, ID, IN, NG, PK, RU and VN), CN rows of the coarse-placer sample, the rendered BD and PK registers, and venue and sub-venue names from the Geofabrik GB, FR, DE and ES extracts plus OSM lexicon entries in `spliced-sub-venue`.

fetch.because: ODbL 3.1 grants a licence to `Use the Database`, and the copyright page states `You are free to copy`. Geofabrik republishes the extracts under ODbL 1.0.

extract.because: ODbL 3.1 grants Use of the Database, which includes Extraction; 4.4(b) states that Extraction of a Substantial part into a new database makes a Derivative Database, which the licence permits on the share-alike condition.

transform.because: The copyright page states `You are free to ... adapt our data`, and ODbL governs the adapted rows as a Derivative Database under 4.4.

train.because: 3.1 grants Use, `explicitly include[s] commercial use, and do[es] not exclude any field of endeavour`. Training on a Derivative Database creates a Produced Work, which 4.5(b) takes outside share-alike, on the 4.3 notice and the 4.6 offer of the Derivative Database.

redistribute-data.because: 4.2 and 4.4 permit Publicly Conveying a Derivative Database only under ODbL 1.0 (or a 4.4(a) compatible licence), with a copy or URI of the licence and the notices kept intact. The training extract is published as `sister-software/mailwoman-osm-training-extract` under ODbL 1.0 with `© OpenStreetMap contributors`. Any other published split or index that contains OSM-derived rows must carry the same terms; it cannot be published under the repository's own licence.

redistribute-model.because: Weights are a Produced Work under the OSMF guideline, so 4.5(b) leaves them outside share-alike. Publicly Using them needs the 4.3 notice that Contents came from OpenStreetMap under ODbL, carried in the model card and rights files, and 4.6 needs the offer of the Derivative Database, met by the published training extract.

commercial-sublicense.because: ODbL 4.8 states `You may not sublicense the Database. Each time You communicate the Database, the whole or Substantial part of the Contents, or any Derivative Database to anyone else in any way, the Licensor offers to the recipient a license to the Database on the same terms and conditions as this License.` A commercial agreement over the weights covers the Produced Work; it cannot grant rights in the OSM data or the extract, which a recipient takes from the OpenStreetMap Foundation under ODbL.

Section III requires changes to be marked in the source statement. No version is stated, so no `spdx` is written. A caution is recorded rather than resolved. extract.because: Section I permits the information to be `prilagođavati`, adapted, which covers reading thoroughfare names, locators, postcodes and settlement names out of the GML.

redistribute-model.because: Section I names exploiting the information `integriranjem u … proizvode i aplikacije u javnim i nejavnim elektroničkim mrežama`, so publishing weights is permitted with the Section II source statement in their rights files.

commercial-sublicense.because: The licence grants an `osobno pravo`, a personal right, to each user, and it states no right to sublicense. A commercial recipient holds the same Open Licence from the publisher directly, on the Section II condition.

It maps `BLK_NO`, `ROAD_NAME`, `BUILDING` and `POSTAL`. That page, 10,945 bytes, sha256 `f976fb3a4d64fe2c5fc76417b955d0ace74d4c0c02091bec50927cf82aa08406`, is the `Singapore Open Data Licence version 1.0`, granting `a worldwide, perpetual, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence`. It states: `You can use, access, download, copy, distribute, transmit, modify and adapt the datasets, or any derived analyses or applications, whether commercially or non-commercially`. It allows a sub-licence `if this is necessary to enable users of your application and/or website … to use your application or access your website`, and states that `This Licence does not grant any rights to Downstream Sub-Licensees`. It excludes `any personal data in the dataset` and third-party rights. It requires `a conspicuous notice acknowledging the source of the datasets and including a link to the most recent version of this Licence`, with an indemnity. OneMap's separate Terms of Use, `https://www.onemap.gov.sg/legal/termsofuse.html`, 31,904 bytes, sha256 `8ccd8eb76df25639cf669f9daba3dc16700e2fffb83729fefde9ea8476dce455`, govern the site and its API. Clause 3(a) grants a `non-transferable, non-exclusive, royalty-free, revocable licence to access, view, download, print or otherwise use the SLA Data … for any usage`, and the next clause forbids modifying, adapting or distributing `Except as expressly permitted in Clause 3(a)`. That restriction governs material taken from the site under the Terms of Use. The OpenAddresses record names the Open Data Licence for this dataset, and this repository reads the Overture rows built from that dataset rather than calling the OneMap API, so the Open Data Licence is elected. A caution is recorded rather than resolved: if a later build fetches from the OneMap API, the Terms of Use govern that copy, and that copy has no adaptation right. No SPDX identifier exists for this licence, so none is written. `training-manifests/v0.7.2-address-systems.effective.json` already names this licence for the Overture Singapore rows.

fetch.because: The licence permits the datasets to be accessed, downloaded and copied, which covers taking the Overture rows built from them.

extract.because: The licence permits the datasets to be modified and adapted, which covers reading block number, road name, building name and postal code.

transform.because: `modify and adapt the datasets, or any derived analyses or applications`, commercially or not, covers rendering rows into components.

train.because: Use is defined to include modifying and adapting for commercial purposes, and the licence carries no share-alike term. Its one exclusion, personal data, is a question for the personal-data review in `source-resolutions.json`.

redistribute-data.because: The licence permits the datasets to be distributed and transmitted, on the condition of the conspicuous source notice with a link to the licence, for example `Contains information from OneMap addresses accessed on <date> from Singapore Land Authority which is made available under the terms of the Singapore Open Data Licence version 1.0`.

redistribute-model.because: The grant extends to `any derived analyses or applications`, so weights may be published with the source notice in their rights files.

commercial-sublicense.because: Only within the licence's own limit. A sub-licence may be granted where `necessary to enable users of your application and/or website … to use your application`, so the users of a shipped model or product are covered. A commercial recipient who redistributes further is a Downstream Sub-Licensee, holds no rights through this repository, and must take the licence from onemap.gov.sg, which the agreement has to say.

licenses.electedBecause: The City of Berkeley states one grant for every dataset on its portal, on its own Open Data Portal page, `https://berkeleyca.gov/your-government/public-records/open-data-portal`, 162,213 bytes, sha256 `02495340b5868dedd4e8a9fcb9ccc72a098764473275a545635df388e02ae17c`: `Explore over 40 datasets available to the public through the City of Berkeley’s Open Data Portal . … You can download, reuse, and redistribute the data from our portal without restrictions.` OpenAddresses' source record `sources/us/ca/city_of_berkeley.json`, 2,660 bytes, sha256 `6c38848d3ab083c932071f94586741a7d80d1e21612816dc1d9b11f6b42e138f`, reads the GeoJSON export of portal dataset `rax9-nuvx` (`TaxParcel2017`), which backs the `bhxd-e6up` Parcels map, and labels its licence `attribution: true`, `attribution name: City of Berkeley`, `presumed: true`; the presumption is OpenAddresses', and the city's page states no attribution condition. The portal's own metadata for `rax9-nuvx`, 33,020 bytes, sha256 `c8d2c2236b63d7ebe64346841ec53d5267dc87deef49712346f4747b8afce5cf`, and for `bhxd-e6up`, 5,303 bytes, sha256 `90fa63966a8529382396bedc059cd31a45f489d9d63d2c62a034b1ce5de88b54`, set no `license` field and give `attribution` `City of Berkeley - Department of Information Technology`, owner `CityofBerkeley`, which proves the file is a dataset `from our portal`. The grant names three acts, download, reuse and redistribution, and qualifies them with `without restrictions`. It does not name adaptation; the election reads `reuse … without restrictions` as covering reading, transforming and training, because a reuse limited to the original form would be a restriction the sentence disclaims. That reading is the decision on which transform and train rest. The dataset description says the parcels are `Sourced from Alameda County Information Technology Department and clipped to City of Berkeley parcels only`; the city's grant covers what its portal publishes, and Alameda County states no separate condition on this copy. The portal's `terms-of-use` path answered 403 to both fetchers, so no further site terms were read. The statement carries no version, so `spdx` and `termsVersion` are left out. Credit `City of Berkeley` in the rights files as a courtesy matching OpenAddresses' record.

licenses.electedTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
licenses.electedBecause: The District states two terms that apply in order, and the dataset's own notice governs. OpenAddresses' source record `sources/us/dc/statewide.json`, 2,406 bytes, sha256 `d63a225a797f764b79d15f5ba2bb740aec8d98a9d34301753a14b6aa64bad9ab`, downloads `https://opendata.dc.gov/api/download/v1/items/aa514416aaf74fdc94748f1e56e7cc8a/geojson?layers=0` and names `https://dc.gov/page/terms-and-conditions-use-district-data` as the licence. That page, 79,353 bytes, sha256 `fc7674c0a514cc3657e9df3284af8d464ced1d1c3e94fbc983de66e843f5063a`, reads: `Unless otherwise noted, the data on the Sites is public domain and made available with a Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal dedication. In short, the District waives all rights to the data worldwide under copyright law … You can copy, modify, distribute, and perform the data, even for commercial purposes, all without asking permission.` and `While not required, we ask that you give proper credit when using data from the Sites in your own work. … Data retrieved from Open Data DC catalog ( https://opendata.dc.gov )`. The item the download names, `aa514416aaf74fdc94748f1e56e7cc8a`, `Address Points`, owner `DCGISopendata`, `accessInformation` `Office of the Chief Technology Officer`, retained as `dc-item-aa514416.json`, 2,871 bytes, sha256 `e582e3ef45a15b0e6b3828207fae103061aec971428dd6c27c1320a9230824b6`, notes otherwise: its `licenseInfo` reads `This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.` linking `https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0`. Because the item is `otherwise noted`, the election is CC BY 4.0, the more conditioned of the two; the operations it permits are a subset of what CC0 would permit, so the reading cannot overstate the grant. CC BY 4.0's legal code, `https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode.en`, 48,742 bytes, sha256 `58230517b7895aa219ff46a6ed63e67057a1582fb9ea054b16728a8c13525650`, §2(a)(1) grants `a worldwide, royalty-free, non-sublicensable, non-exclusive, irrevocable license … to: reproduce and Share the Licensed Material, in whole or in part; and produce, reproduce, and Share Adapted Material`. The credit is `Office of the Chief Technology Officer, District of Columbia, Address Points, Open Data DC (https://opendata.dc.gov), CC BY 4.0, changed`.

fetch.because: CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(1)(A) grants the right to reproduce the material, which covers downloading the GeoJSON export.

extract.because: §2(a)(1)(B) grants producing Adapted Material, which covers reading the address number, street, quadrant, city, state and ZIP columns.

transform.because: §2(a)(1)(B) grants adaptation for any purpose, so a token and tag corpus is permitted with the change indicated under §3(a)(1)(B).

train.because: §2(a)(1)(A) grants reproduction and §2(a)(1)(B) grants producing Adapted Material for any purpose, commercial use included, and fitting a model performs both.

redistribute-data.because: The Share grant covers redistribution in any medium, conditioned on the §3(a) attribution and on adding no restriction beyond the licence.

redistribute-model.because: If trained weights are Adapted Material, §2(a)(1)(B) grants sharing them for any purpose on the §3(a) attribution and change-statement conditions; if they are not, the licence does not reach them. Either way publishing the weights is permitted, with the credit and the statement of changes in the package's rights files.

commercial-sublicense.because: §2(a)(1) grants a `non-sublicensable` licence, so this repository cannot sublicense the material. §2(a)(5)(A) offers every recipient a licence from the Licensor directly, so a commercial recipient takes the District's data from the District on the same credit condition rather than from this repository.

licenses.refusedBecause: The address fields this source reads are the Broadband Serviceable Location Fabric, which the FCC distributes only under a limited end-user licence from its contractor CostQuest, and none of that licence's tiers covers commercial model training. The `fcc-bdc` adapter reads `address_primary`, `city`, `state`, `zip` and `zip_suffix` keyed by `location_id` from a SQLite database built outside this repository (`packages/corpus/lib/us/adapters/fcc-bdc/README.md`). The FCC's help article `How Entities Can Access the Location Fabric`, `https://help.bdc.fcc.gov/hc/en-us/articles/10419121200923-How-Entities-Can-Access-the-Location-Fabric`, read through the help centre's article API as `fcc-zendesk-entities.json`, 8,385 bytes, sha256 `c0657b80e8a4a01e18f24e97d1bd2855f043f33f5cb69a20090e9233ec9d357b` (the HTML page answered 403), states: `The FCC’s National Broadband Map allows users to download data reported by providers on the broadband serviceable locations (or BSLs) they serve and the type of service offered at each BSL. These downloadable data are available by Location ID … To obtain more information about the location beyond its Location ID, such its address, geographic coordinates, and building type, users will need to obtain access to the Fabric.` and `There are two Tier 4 Fabric License Agreements, the Standard Agreement and the Research License. … The Standard Agreement can only be used for the purpose of generating challenge and crowdsource data as part of the Broadband Data Collection . The Tier 4 Research License additionally supports non-commercial academic or public-policy research directly related to broadband availability.` The provider article (`fcc-zendesk-providers.json`, 7,937 bytes, sha256 `7854c01ad2319e7cf4dc085c639b225748e9609986fadb4d6b75fe63a9d4cdc8`) states `each service provider will need to execute a limited end-user license agreement`, scoped to `the counties in which they make broadband internet access service available`, and `Access to and use of the Fabric data will only be allowed via signing the published language in the agreement`; the government article (`fcc-zendesk-government.json`, 7,133 bytes, sha256 `fc85377060c8c380771637b237e6fbe3b5bbc749e62f79633079b62b31b5025a`) scopes government licences to `the counties in their jurisdiction`. So the public download carries no address, and every route to the address fields is a purpose-limited licence: BDC challenges, non-commercial broadband research, or a provider's or government's own service area. Training and publishing a commercially licensed general-purpose address parser is none of these. The adapter's README stamps rows `Public Domain` `per the FCC's federal-government distribution terms`; that holds for the FCC's own Location-ID-level availability files and not for the Fabric's addresses, so the stamp is wrong for every row this adapter emits. No tier the FCC describes reaches this use.

The adapter README's `Public Domain per Hawaii state government open-data terms` is not the publisher's statement about this file. A different artifact exists: Hawaii Open Data's CKAN record `hawaii-public-schools` (id `a761c69f-cfd5-4bd6-a79a-ea4c9cb92788`, organization `Education`) carries `license_id: ocd-by`, author `data.hawaii.gov`, with CSV, RDF, JSON and XML resources last modified 2020-01-10, retained in `hi-ckan-schools.json`, 197,050 bytes, sha256 `8684e3d7809ff58adc5aab17faeb76b708d30109616339b5cfde8f3978c378da`. Its resources are not SchoolList.xlsx, so it licenses that 2020 snapshot rather than the file read here; electing it would mean repointing the adapter at those resources and reading the ODC-By attribution terms. A request to HIDOE's Communications Branch, which the terms page names for logo permissions, could also produce a grant for the workbook.

licenses.electedBecause: The dataset `Commissioned NYS Notaries Public` (`rwbv-mz6z`), attributed to `New York State Department of State (DOS)`, carries no license field of its own in `https://data.ny.gov/api/views/rwbv-mz6z.json`, 31,799 bytes, sha256 `2adad1eae4e6226975d7c4de79422a96694c370912415bcd296b232b871919a4`, so the portal's terms govern. Those are the OPEN-NY Terms of Use, `https://data.ny.gov/download/77gx-ii52/application%2Fpdf`, served as `OPEN-NY Terms of Use.pdf`, 128,817 bytes, sha256 `9437c849705d58df008f01fc23f404444becce6b86676adc3974f9160a4cb650`, `LAST MODIFIED: March 8, 2013`, six pages read in full. The cover page states `use our government information however you wish, in private sector projects` and that the terms `do not contain restrictions requiring members of the public to use attribution, to re-post the license terms with any re-uses of the data, to impose share-alike or technical restrictions, nor require the public to obtain pre-approval before re-use of the data`, and `So long as you are not doing anything malicious with NYS data, you may use it as you wish, subject to no other requirements.` The operative clause under `Intellectual Property` is `The State grants you a non-exclusive, revocable license to use the Content contained on this website in a manner consistent with the Terms of Use`, and the adaptation verbs appear only as a limit on use `inconsistent with the Terms of Use`: `you will not reproduce, modify, adapt, prepare derivative works based on … OPEN-NY Content in a manner inconsistent with the Terms of Use`. Three conditions carry forward. The license is revocable: `Upon termination, all licenses and other rights granted to you in these Terms of Use will immediately cease`. `Any rights not expressly granted herein are reserved.` And use must be lawful, including compliance with intellectual property laws. The rows name individual notaries with business addresses; the terms state that content `has been vetted by the government agencies supplying the Content in order to reasonably ensure that information protected from disclosure by law is not released`, and impose no personal-data condition beyond lawful use, so that question belongs to this source's personal-data review, which `source-resolutions.json` does not yet hold.

extract.because: The license is `to use the Content`, and reading columns out of the export is use.

transform.because: The terms forbid modification and derivative works only `in a manner inconsistent with the Terms of Use`, and the cover page states the terms impose no share-alike and no pre-approval, so a lawful derived corpus is consistent with them.

train.because: `use our government information however you wish, in private sector projects`; fitting a model is a lawful private-sector use.

licenses.refusedBecause: OpenAddresses grants no licence over the address data it collects, so the collection row has no grant of its own to elect. The repository README, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openaddresses/openaddresses/master/README.md`, 5,259 bytes, sha256 `beccea446f8a31b4eb67b5dd4104edccd4a8bb217cec0c918308d6c9ba394138`, states under `License`: `The data produced by the OpenAddresses processing pipeline (available on [batch.openaddresses.io](https://batch.openaddresses.io/)) is not relicensed from the original sources. Individual sources will have their own licenses. The OpenAddresses team does its best to summarize the source licenses in the source JSON for each source.` and `The source JSON in this repo (in the sources/ directory) is licensed under the CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication ... The rest of the repository is licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License`. The BSD licence, 1,480 bytes, sha256 `0166cd89016fcfb1e1b1ed736507a384865e875c5bb7ee7bd07545312f50a3ee`, and `sources/LICENSE`, 419 bytes, sha256 `9e90a0117df55c4dd3f1bace28c79a25da71832035f3d7304548d573cc627a22`, cover the code and the source definitions, not the addresses. The home page, `https://openaddresses.io/`, 5,667 bytes, sha256 `89bb7f62b4909531277b9e3bb567e1f253c24352716862d067013ff48be9fccd`, states `OpenAddresses is open data . All data is openly licensed. Most sources only require attribution.`, which is the aggregator's characterisation of other publishers' licences, not a grant. `https://batch.openaddresses.io/`, 1,171 bytes, sha256 `b195777427a49dcb207d6f419b9b55c773906851adc105852d737ccbb48714ef`, is an application shell with no terms. The permission for any OpenAddresses row is its source's, and each source carries its own decision in this register keyed by that publisher. That route needs the source of each row: the `openaddresses` adapter reads batch collections `whose per-row upstream the adapter does not record`, and `fragment-assay` and `oa-slavic` record no file either, so no row read through this collection can reach a per-source decision today. Overture's attribution page shows the collection is not uniform: it lists OpenAddresses-distributed sources under `a non-exclusive, limited, and revocable license` (Allegan, Kent and Muskegon counties, Michigan) and Portugal's INE with no licence named. Recording each row's source (the OpenAddresses source definition, whose JSON names the source's licence) and electing that publisher's licence admits those rows; for the US skeletons in `invented-house-venue` (31.5%) and `spliced-sub-venue`, the county and state bodies need the same per-source record.

licenses.electedBecause: This is the reading recorded for `unchecked-access-free-gb-who-s-on-first`, applied to every jurisdiction the corpus reads. The two documents retrieved today are byte-identical to that decision's copies. The data repository's `LICENSE.md`, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whosonfirst/whosonfirst-data/master/LICENSE.md`, 725 bytes, sha256 `634276f100c598a3f8b79250a852383278857868a2d5efcf6639d485ae4a2cb0`, states: `Crediting Who's On First is recommended and linking back to the License is required. For example: > Data from Who's On First. [License](https://whosonfirst.org/docs/licenses/).`, then `The Who's On First dataset is both an original work and a modification of existing open data. Some of those open data projects do require attribution.`, and puts `The format and structure that allows Who's On First to operate` under a Creative Commons Zero designation. The licences page, `https://whosonfirst.org/docs/licenses/`, 48,404 bytes, sha256 `bb584e412810ef475b32264bf1d2b5c12f188006d5929b9441f56c2b5ddfc0ed`, repeats that text and lists 102 contributing sources, each with its own licence link. The links are open-data licences in the large majority (CC BY 2.0/2.5/3.0/4.0, CC0, OGL v2.0 and v3.0, the Canadian federal, provincial and municipal open government licences, DL-DE BY 2.0, Licence Ouverte, Swisstopo's free geodata conditions, the Census Bureau's terms, GeoNames under CC BY 4.0, Quattroshapes under CC BY 2.0, Natural Earth's public-domain terms). A few link a site-wide copyright page rather than a data licence: ISO's and ITU's copyright pages, which carry country and region codes, and Wikipedia's copyright page, whose text is CC BY-SA. The statement reserves nothing and names the link as its one required condition. It grants no licence of its own over Mapzen's original work beyond the format and structure, so this election reads the statement as permission conditioned on the link, together with the sources' own grants, and the credit set is the whole 102-source list because the admin database records a geometry source per record and no name source. What this repository reads under this row: place names, placetypes and parent ids from the WOF admin SQLite for locality, county and region tuples (`invented-house-venue-v063`, `invented-no-street`, `invented-no-street-v063`, `invented-po-box`), CN rows of the coarse-placer sample, locality spans in `fragment-assay`, seed rows of the `deepseek-translit-*` recipes, and US ZIP codes from `postalcode-us.db` in `invented-anchor-absorption`. A place name, a placetype, a parent relation and a ZIP code are facts each source also states; none of these reads copies a source's descriptive text.

fetch.because: The project publishes the bundles and databases for download and states the link as its one required condition. The contributing sources' licences grant copying.

extract.because: The statement describes the dataset as a modification of open data and reserves nothing. The contributing sources' licences grant adaptation, which covers reading place names, placetypes, parent ids and postal codes out of the databases.

transform.because: Joining a place to its parents and writing locality, county and region tuples adapts the records, which the contributing licences grant on their attribution conditions (for example CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(1)(B), OGL v3.0 `adapt the Information`).

train.because: The Who's On First statement adds only the link, and the contributing open licences permit commercial use with attribution. Using place tuples as training rows is a use those grants cover.

redistribute-data.because: A published corpus split or index that carries the place tuples must carry `Data from Who's On First. License: https://whosonfirst.org/docs/licenses/` and the contributing sources' credits, which the licences page lists. CC BY-SA text from Wikipedia does not reach a row: the rows carry names and codes, not article text.

redistribute-model.because: Every contributing open licence permits including the data in a product, and the Who's On First statement requires only the link, which the weights packages' rights files carry.

commercial-sublicense.because: The statement grants no licence of its own that this repository could pass on, and the CC BY sources are not sublicensable (CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(1) grants a `non-sublicensable` licence). Each grant is made to every recipient directly, so a commercial recipient takes the data on the link and credit conditions from Who's On First and its sources rather than from this repository.

licenses.electedBecause: The publisher's own catalogue record is the grant. On catalogodatos.gub.uy the dataset `Direcciones Geográficas del Uruguay` sits in the organization `ide`, the Infraestructura de Datos Espaciales, with `license_id: odc-uy` and a `license_url` that is the licence PDF on gub.uy (`uy-ckan-direcciones.json`, `uy-licencia-datos-abiertos.pdf`). The record's resources are the nineteen department CSVs the `ide-uy` adapter reads, matched by URL in `/mnt/mw/corpus/sources/ide-uy/package_show.json` and each file's receipt. The licence names no SPDX identifier, which is why none is recorded. Its Autorización clause grants, `para uso comercial y no comercial`, that the data `podrán ser: enajenados, reproducidos, distribuidos, publicados, traducidos, adaptados, transformados, comunicados o puestos a disposición del público mediante cualquier forma o procedimiento; fusionados con datos propios y de terceros, pudiendo combinarse para formar conjuntos de datos nuevos e independientes; integrados en los procesos de negocio, productos y aplicaciones internas y externas`. The Nota de Origen clause conditions all of it: cite `el nombre del proveedor`, `la referencia a la "Licencia de Datos Abiertos – Uruguay"` and `la referencia al conjunto de datos que está siendo utilizado`, and `Los cambios, las ediciones, los nuevos diseños o modificaciones deben ser mencionados en la nota de origen`.

fetch.because: The Autorización clause grants that the data may be `reproducidos`, which is what copying the published CSVs performs.

extract.because: The clause grants that the data may be `adaptados, transformados` and `combinarse para formar conjuntos de datos nuevos e independientes`, which covers reading the address fields out of it.

transform.because: The clause grants adaptation and transformation, and the Nota de Origen requires that changes `deben ser mencionados`, so the obligation is a disclosure rather than a restriction. The adapter re-renders each point as an address line, drops unnamed streets and route-kilometre points, and omits the rural-remainder census locality, which the note of origin states.

train.because: The clause grants that the data may be `integrados en los procesos de negocio, productos y aplicaciones internas y externas`, for commercial use, which is the act a model fitted on the rows performs.

redistribute-data.because: The clause grants that the data may be `distribuidos, publicados` and `puestos a disposición del público mediante cualquier forma o procedimiento`, conditioned on the Nota de Origen naming the provider, the licence and the dataset.

redistribute-model.because: The text grants both acts a weight release could be read as, integration into a product and distribution of a new data set, the second under the Nota de Origen. No release has yet been checked against that note's three citations and its disclosure of changes, so the operation is left for the release that ships these rows.

Clause 12(c) states `Asnjë përdorues nuk mund të kopjojë, modifikojë, publikojë, transmetojë, transferojë ose shesë, riprodhojë, krijojë vepra derivative, shpërndajë, shfaqë ose në ndonjë mënyrë të shfrytëzojë ndonjë nga përmbajtjet, tërësisht ose pjesërisht, me përjashtim i) kur ju lejohet me ligjet dhe rregulloret e prokurimit publik të Republikës së Kosovës, ose ii) me marrëveshjen e shprehur me shkrim të KRPP-së`: no user may copy, modify, publish, transmit, transfer, sell, reproduce, create derivative works from, distribute or display any of the contents, in whole or in part, except where the Republic of Kosovo's public procurement law permits it or by the express written agreement of the KRPP. Copying, extracting and fitting a model are each among the reserved acts. Two limits on this reading are recorded rather than resolved. The document governs the e-procurement portal and names the OCDS export nowhere, so whether the export is `contents in this system` is a reading rather than a statement; the export is a rendering of the portal's own records, which is why the refusal is taken as covering it. And clause 12(c)(ii) names a route to permission, so a written request to the KRPP could reverse this. The register's earlier record rested on the OCP Data Registry reading `License: -`, which is a third party's empty field rather than the publisher's statement, and this replaces it with the publisher's own words.
