sources.coverage: Matrikkelen - Adresse for area 2100 Svalbard, the same dataset Kartverket publishes for the mainland, taken from the dataset's own area list rather than from a separate product. `Basisdata_2100_Svalbard_4258_MatrikkelenAdresse_CSV.zip` is 58,079 bytes, sha256 `71f348ba6f0aeb7b3fb111b17616e1cd33ccf28d08129a70d538db317180727d`, and its member `matrikkelenAdresse.csv` is 321,491 bytes dated 2026-09-08. **Measured 1,096 data rows on 2026-10-01** over the mainland file's same 46 columns, with every row holding exactly 46 fields. `adressetype` reads `vegadresse` on all 1,096, so this extract carries no `matrikkeladresse` cadastral reference, where the mainland file carries 34,522 of them. `kommunenummer` reads `2100 SVALBARD` on every row and `postnummer` reads `9170 LONGYEARBYEN` on every row, so the publication is one settlement rather than the archipelago: Barentsburg, Ny-Ålesund and Sveagruva have no rows here. Longyearbyen's streets are numbered rather than named, so `adresseTekst` reads `Vei 223 8`, `Vei 500 1` and `Vei 608 7`, which is a street-name vocabulary worth knowing before a parser is scored on it. **This row covers Svalbard and not Jan Mayen**, although ISO 3166-1 assigns `SJ` to both: Geonorge's 375-area codelist for this dataset carries no Jan Mayen entry.

personalDataReview.because: The mainland extract's 46 columns were read in full for `no-property-building-1` and none is an owner, occupant, holder or contact. This file declares the same 46, read from the file rather than assumed, so that finding transfers. The two columns that needed their own measurement there were measured again here. **`adressetilleggsnavn`, the free-text name an address may carry, is populated on 0 of the 1,096 rows**, and `adressetilleggsnavnKilde` likewise, so the column that carries Switzerland's class of risk is empty throughout this publication rather than merely low. `organisasjonsnummer` is populated on all 1,096 rows with the single municipality 2100's own value, which identifies a legal entity and is the class this repository carries. The remaining populated name columns are place names: `kommunenavn` `SVALBARD`, `adressenavn` the numbered street, `grunnkretsnavn`, `soknenavn` and `valgkretsnavn` the statistical, parish and electoral units. `tettstednavn` is populated on 0 rows.

sources.name: Base Adresse Nationale — department 988
sources.authorityBasis: Same national geographic institute and same reference database as the metropolitan extract; BAN publishes one file per INSEE department code
sources.access: direct download; gzipped CSV per department updated daily
sources.publisher: Institut national de l'information géographique et forestière (IGN)
sources.note: Measured 51702 rows over 23 columns on 2026-10-01, 7 communes and 7 postcodes.
sources.coverage: Base Adresse Nationale department 988, New Caledonia, at `https://adresse.data.gouv.fr/data/ban/adresses/latest/csv/adresses-988.csv.gz`, 1,446,155 gzipped bytes. **Measured 51,702 rows on 2026-10-01** over the same 23 columns as the national extract, every row holding exactly 23 fields. 7 communes and 7 postcodes: 98800, 98809, 98817, 98825, 98835, 98859 and 98889. New Caledonia has 33 communes, so this publication covers 7 of them and is partial in a way the row count alone does not show. `https://api-adresse.data.gouv.fr/search/` returns `Rue Jacques Iekawe 98800 Nouméa` as `type` `street` with `context` `988, Nouvelle-Calédonie`. Samples: `10 Rue des Sapins, 98825 Pouembout` and `149 Rue des Sapins, 98825 Pouembout`.

personalDataReview.because: The publisher characterises its own content in article 1 of its conditions of use: the BAN holds `la correspondance entre adresse non nominative (numéro, nom de voie, lieu-dit et commune) et position géographique`. This file's header was read from the file rather than assumed from the national extract, and it declares the same 23 columns: `id`, `id_fantoir`, `numero`, `rep`, `nom_voie`, `code_postal`, `code_insee`, `nom_commune`, `code_insee_ancienne_commune`, `nom_ancienne_commune`, `x`, `y`, `lon`, `lat`, `type_position`, `alias`, `nom_ld`, `libelle_acheminement`, `nom_afnor`, `source_position`, `source_nom_voie`, `certification_commune` and `cad_parcelles`. Every row holds exactly 23 fields, so no row introduces a column the header omits, and none of the 23 is an owner, occupant, holder or contact. The six columns whose names begin `nom` were each checked, because a name column is where a party would appear: `nom_voie`, `nom_commune`, `nom_ancienne_commune`, `nom_ld` and `nom_afnor` hold a street, commune or locality name, and `source_nom_voie` names the body that supplied the street name. **A street name commemorating a person is a toponym the commune assigned rather than a record about a resident**, which is why `Rue Gaston Monnerville` in French Guiana and `Rue Madi Mwamba` in Mayotte do not make this reading `present`; the test this register applies is whether a row identifies who is at the address. `cad_parcelles` references a cadastral parcel rather than whoever holds it.

sources.name: INSPIRE - Addresses (Brussels-Capital Region)
sources.authorityBasis: Regional informatics centre of the Brussels-Capital Region and publisher of the UrbIS reference data; publishes the INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme for the region as a bare HTTPS download
sources.access: direct download; one zipped GML for the whole region with no ATOM feed for this theme
sources.note: The ISO 19139 record 260abd6f-c5b4-4a79-aa80-d6c265002d65 states useConstraints CC-BY-4.0 and accessConstraints noLimitations, and names this archive as its distribution. Paradigm's other address product, the BeSt Brussels register in record a8c9ccde-5c2b-11ed-913a-900f0cda5d5c, is CC0-1.0 and carries an ATOM feed; the two are separate publications under separate licenses. Measured 225660 ad:Address, 6238 ad:ThoroughfareName, 26 ad:PostalDescriptor and 23 ad:AdminUnitName on 2026-10-02, reconciling against 231947 gml:featureMember elements. The archive's last-modified is 2022-12-01.
sources.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of Paradigm, reached as a bare HTTPS download at `https://urbisdownload.datastore.brussels/INSPIRE/URBIS_ADM_Adresses.zip`, 11,521,182 bytes, whose single member `UrbAdm_Adresses.gml` is 474,245,978 bytes. **Coverage is the Brussels-Capital Region rather than Belgium**: Flanders publishes its own service and Wallonia publishes separately, so this row is the third of three a Belgian build needs and it sits beside `be-property-building-1` and `be-property-building-2` for that reason. Brussels publishes no INSPIRE ATOM feed for this theme, so there is no `<updated>` element to poll and the download is a bare URL; the archive's `last-modified` is `Thu, 01 Dec 2022 07:57:50 GMT`, which makes it the oldest of the three Belgian regional publications. **Measured 225,660 `ad:Address` features over the whole member rather than a sample**, by `inspire-element-census.run.ts`, which counted all 48 distinct element names the file uses. It carries its components in the same file: 6,238 `ad:ThoroughfareName`, 26 `ad:PostalDescriptor` and 23 `ad:AdminUnitName`, and it publishes no `ad:AddressAreaName`, so a build needs no second request to resolve a component. The counts reconcile, which is the check that the census read the file rather than its own chunk boundaries: 225,660 addresses plus 6,287 component features equals the 231,947 `gml:featureMember` elements, and 231,947 is also the count of `gml:identifier`, `ad:inspireId`, `base:localId`, `ad:beginLifespanVersion` and `ad:validFrom`, one per member. The region is bilingual and the file records it: 12,476 `ad:ThoroughfareNameValue` over 6,238 thoroughfare-name features is exactly two spellings per street, and `gn:language` appears 12,574 times.

personalDataReview.because: Every element name the file ever uses was counted over all 474,245,978 decoded bytes of the member, so this is a denominator of the whole publication rather than a sample of its features. The file uses 48 distinct element names and **`ad:locatorName` is not among them: it appears 0 times, as does `ad:LocatorName`**. That element is the free-text `GeographicalName` through which a family name or a business name reaches an INSPIRE address, and this publisher never writes it. The 24,998 `ad:name` elements and 52 `ad:postName` elements sum to 25,050, which equals the 12,574 `gn:GeographicalName` plus 12,476 `ad:ThoroughfareNameValue` the file carries, and those sit on the component features rather than on an address: 6,238 thoroughfare names, 26 postal descriptors and 23 administrative-unit names, all of them place names. The census ran through `inspireGMLChunks`, the same reader the adapter uses, carrying the text after each chunk's final `<` into the next chunk and decoding with a stateful decoder, so neither a split tag nor a split multi-byte character could hide an occurrence.

sources.name: Rețea școlară (school network)
sources.authorityBasis: The ministry's list of every education unit for a school year, with street, number, postcode and locality
sources.note: The 2025-2026 workbook lists 18,022 units, of which 17,533 carry a street or a house number. Every unit is a public education body, so no row is a natural person's address.
sources.coverage: The 2025-2026 workbook on data.gov.ro, 3,022,486 bytes, sha256 `35cb33c83752a6ac6334f1bd43a8bd53e9573684f949047aa05bd72056971a32`, one sheet `Export` whose header is the fourth row. Measured on 2026-10-03: 18,022 education units. 17,533 carry a street or a house number and become rows; 489 state neither and are refused. 16,393 of the 17,533 carry a house number, and 17,484 of the 18,022 carry a six-digit postcode. `Numar` writes `FN` (`fără număr`) for a premise without a number on about 600 units, which the adapter reads as absent.

personalDataReview.because: Every row is an education unit of the Romanian state system: schools, kindergartens, children's clubs, school inspectorates and teacher centres, 17,433 of 18,022 typed `Unitate de învățământ`. The address is the unit's own premises. The workbook names no natural person in any address-bearing row; the `Email` and `Telefon` columns hold the unit's contact and are not read.

sources.name: CORDIS organisation files (FP7 / Horizon 2020 / Horizon Europe participants)
sources.authorityBasis: The participant register's address for every legal entity in an EU research framework project, across 158 countries
sources.access: bulk CSV zip per programme from cordis.europa.eu
sources.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
sources.note: 420,811 participation rows reduce to 78,842 distinct published records and 57,930 emitted addresses. The participant register holds legal entities; a name rule refuses the 202 records written as a person's name.
sources.coverage: The `organization.csv` members of the CORDIS FP7 (32,953,397 bytes, sha256 `886ee479…`), Horizon 2020 (55,219,250 bytes, `d4a8e364…`) and Horizon Europe (36,908,998 bytes, `1496a16e…`) archives, fetched 2026-10-03. 420,811 participation rows reduce to 78,842 distinct published records (name, street, postcode, city, country) and 57,930 emitted addresses across 158 countries. Refusals: a digit the street split could not place 14,438 and 4,646, no locality 564, a non-ISO country 359, a country without a codex layout 353, too few components 349, a name written as a person's 202. Largest countries: DE 7,967, IT 6,365, ES 4,242, FR 4,055, NL 3,800, GB 3,658.

personalDataReview.because: The participant register enrols legal entities, and `activityType` takes only HES, PRC, REC, OTH, PUB or empty, so no field marks a natural person. A sole trader can register, so the adapter refuses a participant whose name takes a person's form (surname-first uppercase name, a German `e.Kfr.` suffix): 202 of 78,842 distinct records, among them `FISK ADRIAN` and `Melina Bucher e.Kfr.`. A sole trader trading under a business name passes that test, which is the residual exposure this reading records.

sources.name: Valsts adrešu reģistrs (State Address Register) open data
sources.authorityBasis: The national register of building and land-unit addresses, with each address's official written form
sources.note: aw_eka.csv holds 610,876 rows, 550,652 active; the adapter emits 550,637 with the register's own STD string as the written form.
sources.coverage: The 2026-09-30 edition of `varis-atvertie-dati` on data.gov.lv. `aw_eka.csv`, building and land-unit addresses, sha256 `e99669fe0a102d833129559cbeb688ad3c1582d0a52346cb9accb523c41caada`, holds 610,876 rows: 550,652 active (`EKS`), 32,448 removed (`DEL`) and 27,776 erroneous (`ERR`). The adapter emits 550,637, refusing 15 house names written where a street address's number goes. By shape: rural named house in a parish 116,225, street address in a municipality town 113,905, street address in a state city 111,217, named house in a village 108,164, street address in a village 98,179, named house in a city 2,947. Every emitted row's `raw` is the register's `STD` string, which the adapter's join of the parent tables reproduces on all 550,637. `aw_dziv.csv` (868,669 active premises in 57,285 buildings) is not read.

personalDataReview.because: The address register records addresses and the codes of their parent places, and names no owner, resident or occupant. A rural house name such as `Riņņi` is the premise's registered name rather than a person's. No field ties an address to a natural person.

sources.name: GLEIF Level 1 LEI golden copy
sources.authorityBasis: The legal and headquarters addresses of every LEI holder, validated against local registration authorities
sources.access: daily bulk CSV zip from goldencopy.gleif.org
sources.note: The 2026-10-03 08:00 publish holds 3,451,350 records; the adapter emits 1,356,108 distinct addresses across 178 countries after refusing sole proprietors and lines it cannot label.
sources.coverage: The 2026-10-03 08:00 Level 1 golden copy, `20261003-0800-gleif-goldencopy-lei2-golden-copy.csv.zip`, 507,006,221 bytes, sha256 `8b56eca84ea750dd343a69ffd837f1ba6738bb063167e24d00192f0127d47d03`, 3,451,350 records. The headquarters address repeats the legal address on 2,755,787 records and is read once. The adapter emits 1,356,108 distinct addresses across 178 countries; the largest are DE 178,755, IT 153,146, NL 147,226, US 137,213 and FR 102,618. The largest address refusals are a street number it cannot place 873,601, a care-of first line 645,366 and a first line with no digit 301,531. AE, HK and BS rows are refused as unreviewed, because their sampled rows mislabel office numbers, floors and suite markers.

personalDataReview.because: LEI holders are legal entities, but GLEIF registers sole proprietors too. The adapter refuses 131,148 records as natural persons: `EntityCategory` `SOLE_PROPRIETOR` 129,552, an ELF code naming a sole-proprietorship form 382, and a free-text legal form naming a sole trader 1,214. `MailRouting`, which holds care-of lines naming people, is never read, and a first line written as care of a person is refused. A sole trader registered under a non-sole-proprietor category and a business name passes, which is the residual exposure.

sources.name: Active MOT test stations
sources.authorityBasis: DVSA authorises and lists every premises approved to carry out MOT tests in Great Britain
sources.note: Columns Site_Number, Trading_Name, Address1, Address2, Address3, Town, Postcode, Phone and six vehicle-class flags. The file read on 2026-10-12 is 2,391,015 bytes with 22,988 lines including the header.
sources.coverage: DVSA's active MOT test stations CSV, `https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6abcee45943e890cb55e5d00/active-mot-stations.csv`, read 2026-10-12: 2,391,015 bytes, sha256 `1feeed6fa09140db3cde595c59b0503aa597cdc75a4846444c11122a6e5241c4`, 22,988 data rows over 14 columns with 0 ragged rows under a quote-aware parse; 923 lines carry a quote character. One row is one approved test premises. 22,969 of 22,988 postcodes take a valid Great Britain postcode shape and 121 postcode areas are present, including AB 217, EH 309 and G 369 in Scotland and CF 386, SA 342 and LL 282 in Wales; BT, Northern Ireland, has 0 rows, because Northern Ireland tests vehicles through its own agency. 7,126 rows open `Address1` with a digit, so about a third carry a house number and the rest open with a building, unit or estate name.

personalDataReview.because: The address columns locate test premises, and the `Trading_Name` column names a natural person on some rows. Among 22,988 trading names, 235 take an initial-and-surname shape without a business word, as `J J GRIFFITHS`, `R C WILSON`, `V WILLIAMS` and `S BISHOP` do, and 106 carry `AND SON` or `& SONS`, some of which are limited companies. A sole trader's name beside the premises where that person trades identifies them, which is the reading this register gave Enhetsregisteret's sole proprietorships. The shape count is a lower bound. **Whether a build that reads only the five address columns and never `Trading_Name` changes this reading is the same open question recorded for swisstopo's `BDG_NAME`**, and it is the operator's and counsel's to answer: an approved MOT premises is a commercial site with test equipment, so the address alone locates a business.

sources.name: Code-Point Open
sources.authorityBasis: Ordnance Survey publishes a coordinate for every current Great Britain postcode unit, built from Royal Mail's PAF and the GridLink consortium dataset

Columns are postcode, positional quality, easting, northing and GSS codes; there is no street, post town or locality name. The licence file adds Royal Mail and National Statistics acknowledgements.
sources.coverage: OS Code-Point Open, 2026-08 release, `codepo_gb.zip` sha256 `fc266d063e4d8c27bd23ea8a65c6855162942cf6b9fc73c91d0930d442a0eefb`, read 2026-10-14: 120 postcode-area CSV files, 1,749,109 rows, 10 columns (`Postcode,Positional_quality_indicator,Eastings,Northings,Country_code,NHS_regional_HA_code,NHS_HA_code,Admin_county_code,Admin_district_code,Admin_ward_code`), no header row. Great Britain only: 0 rows begin `BT`. The file carries no post town, locality or street. In the LS area, 22,197 of 22,198 postcodes carry coordinates, and 21,648 of those 22,197 (97.53%) lie within 100 m of a named OS Open Roads link; 903 share a coordinate with another postcode. The `gb-os-open` adapter also reads `gb-public-administration-2` (OS Open Names) and `gb-transport-1` (OS Open Roads), which share the license decision `ogl-uk-3.0-gb-ordnance-survey-opendata` and each record `absent` personal data.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap
sources.authorityBasis: The OpenStreetMap Foundation holds the database that OpenStreetMap contributors edit and publishes it under the ODbL 1.0

sources.name: Overture Maps addresses and places themes
sources.authorityBasis: Overture Maps Foundation compiles address points from national, state and municipal publishers and from OpenAddresses, and places of interest from Meta, Microsoft and other contributors
sources.access: GeoParquet releases on the Overture S3 and Azure buckets
sources.note: The addresses theme is read by the overture adapter, the Singapore register recipe, the Japan and Taiwan corpora and their register alignment, and through the US situs databases behind the house-venue and sub-venue tuples; each upstream publisher's terms travel with its rows. The places theme is read for venue names by the venue and sub-venue recipes, through place-names/names.parquet and poi.db. The divisions theme, ODbL 1.0, reaches the corpus through the admin gazetteer's Overture fold: the trailing-region recipes join postcodes to localities in that database, and for Canada and the other countries the fold covers, the locality and region names can be Overture rows.

sources.name: Federal Register of Buildings and Dwellings (GWR) building addresses, through OpenAddresses ch/countrywide
sources.authorityBasis: The BFS keeps the GWR under the VGWR (SR 431.841) and publishes its access level A data, which include streets and building addresses
sources.access: OpenAddresses ch/countrywide as run in 2021, whose source at openaddresses/openaddresses e880e070c5f1 downloaded https://data.geo.admin.ch/ch.bfs.gebaeude_wohnungs_register/CSV/CH/CH.zip
sources.note: The on-disk openaddresses/extracted/ch/countrywide.csv is dated 2021-10-17. OpenAddresses switched ch/countrywide to swisstopo's official building address directory only on 2024-11-22 (520f9ebf45a6), so the file the rendered-ch and fragment-assay recipes read is this BFS publication rather than ch-property-building-1.

sources.name: Direcciones Geográficas del Uruguay
sources.authorityBasis: The IDE, the national spatial data infrastructure under Presidencia de la República, publishes the national geographic address points
sources.access: One CSV per department on catalogodatos.gub.uy, CKAN dataset `ide-direcciones-geograficas-del-uruguay` in the organization `ide`
sources.note: Read by the ide-uy adapter. 1,059,247 address points across 19 department files retrieved 2026-10-17, each with postcode, street, door number and census locality.
sources.coverage: Direcciones Geográficas del Uruguay, nineteen CSVs, one per department, from the CKAN dataset `ide-direcciones-geograficas-del-uruguay` of the organization `ide` on catalogodatos.gub.uy, metadata modified 2026-10-01 and retrieved 2026-10-17. **Measured 1,059,247 address points** by parsing every file: Montevideo 386,986, Canelones 171,140, Maldonado 57,656, Colonia 49,161 and the other fifteen departments between 10,102 (Flores) and 37,708 (Paysandú). Every row carries `codigo_postal`, `nombre_via` and `departamento`; `num_puerta` is present on 1,057,744, `localidad` on 1,059,164, `letra_puerta` on 30,103, `km` on 1,361, `manzana` on 524,558 and `nombre_inmueble` on 904. 47,486 rows of the adapter's output name a census locality `<DEPARTAMENTO> RURAL`, the department's rural remainder, and 25,504 name a generated code (`UYARMQA_SN_012`) where the street is unnamed. **The files are Windows-1252, not UTF-8**, and a street holding a nickname is quoted with doubled quotes (`"AVENIDA JOSE ""PEPE"" D' ELIA"`), so a reader that splits on `,` misaligns nine Montevideo lines.

personalDataReview.because: The fifteen columns were read in full, and fourteen are address structure: a position, a postcode, a street code and name, a door number and letter, a route kilometre, a block and lot, a census locality and its code, and the department. `nombre_inmueble`, the building name, is free text on 904 rows. Read by its leading words, it names post offices (`AG OFICIAL CORREO` 128, `SUC CORREO` 103), police stations (`SECCIONAL`), municipal and ministry buildings, and holiday houses (`CHALET LA`, `CHALET MARIA`). Three rows name a mail distribution agent by the agent's own name (`Agente Distribucion` followed by a person's given and family names), which is a natural person's name at an address. The `ide-uy` adapter refuses those values (`component:venue:names-a-person`) and every value without a three-letter word, so no person's name reaches a row; a holiday house's given name (`CHALET MARIA`) names the property rather than identifying anyone.

sources.name: Verzeichnis der Gebäudeadressen
sources.authorityBasis: The Landesverwaltung keeps the official index of building addresses (amtliches Gebäudeadressverzeichnis) and publishes it on its geodata download service
sources.access: One ZIP (`dataset.csv` and a shapefile) from `https://service.geo.llv.li/download//getfile.php?theme=officialAdress`, listed on `https://service.geo.llv.li/download/`
sources.note: Read by the llv-li adapter. 12,966 address rows in `dataset.csv` retrieved 2026-10-18, each with street, number, postcode, postal locality and coordinates.
sources.coverage: Verzeichnis der Gebäudeadressen, one ZIP from service.geo.llv.li (`officialAdress.zip`, 1,306,445 bytes, sha256 `ea8592ccc2ef85a7db73473e5a21ac62be5a3b39bba6f16dcea597636983bcea`) retrieved 2026-10-18, holding `dataset.csv` (2,049,756 bytes) and a shapefile. **Measured 12,966 address rows** by parsing the whole CSV, which is Windows-1252, `;`-separated and unquoted. `STATUS` reads `real` on 12,733 and `planned` on 233, and `OFFICIAL` reads `FALSE` on 4. Every row carries `STN_NAME`, `ADR_NUMBER`, `ZIP_ZIP4` and `ZIP_NAME`; no two rows share street, number and postcode. The 13 postal localities and 13 postcodes cover all eleven municipalities. No column names the municipality, only its number (`COM_FOSNR`). The `llv-li` adapter writes 12,729 rows and refuses the planned and unofficial ones.

personalDataReview.because: The twenty columns were read in full: identifiers of the address, street, building and entrance (`ADR_EGAID`, `STR_ESID`, `BDG_EGID`, `ADR_EDID`, `FL_GEID`, `AV_STRNR`), the street name and number, the municipality number, the postcode and postal locality, status flags, coordinates in two systems and a modification date. None is a free-text name column, and none identifies an owner, occupant or contact.

sources.name: Land transactions
sources.authorityBasis: The Land Registry records every registered transfer of land on the Isle of Man and publishes the transactions as open data
sources.access: A monthly CSV on www.gov.im; the host answers 403 from the lab host, and the January 2025 file is read from the Internet Archive's capture
sources.note: Read by the landregistry-im adapter, which keeps only the address columns and emits each distinct address once. 40,847 transactions and 26,748 distinct addresses in `landtransactionsjan2025.csv`.
sources.coverage: Land transactions, the Isle of Man Land Registry's CSV `landtransactionsjan2025.csv` (4,128,696 bytes, sha256 `9b6ec3801347e48ed1b53d95db7331b0c1e30a5786c4ee364d29d8500d9cc760`), read from the Internet Archive's 2025-02-23 capture because www.gov.im answered 403 to the live file on 2026-10-18. **Measured 40,847 transactions** with completion dates from 2000-11-06 to 2025-01-31, all twelve fields wide, no line breaks inside fields. Street_Name is present on 40,842, House_Number on 22,692, House_Name on 18,948, SubUnit_Name on 6,585, Locality on 10,033 and Postcode on 37,386. Each row is a sale, so an address repeats once per sale: 26,742 distinct addresses by the raw address fields, case-folded. Land without a building appears as a description (`Field North Of Ballawhannel Farm`). The `landregistry-im` adapter keeps only the address columns, emits each address once and refuses land parcels and non-premises (garages, plots, substations), writing 21,655 rows.

personalDataReview.because: The twelve columns were read in full. Seven are address structure (`SubUnit_Name`, `House_Number`, `House_Name`, `Street_Name`, `Locality`, `Town`, `Postcode`, plus `Parish_`), and four describe the sale (`Market_Value`, `Consideration`, `Acquisition_Date`, `CompletionDate`). The dataset page states that the purchaser's name `has not been included`, and no column names a buyer, seller or occupant. A sale price at a dated address is information about a transaction rather than a person, and the adapter does not read the price or date columns, so no row carries them. `House_Name` holds a house's given name (`Starvold`, `The Rhullick`, `El Pozo`), which names the property; the adapter refuses values that hold a number or describe land rather than name a building.

sources.name: Freeport address points
sources.authorityBasis: The Grand Bahama Port Authority administers the City of Freeport under the Hawksbill Creek Agreement and assigns its street addresses
sources.access: CSV, GeoJSON, SQL and shapefile copies in the GitHub repository `GBPA/gis-datafiles`
sources.note: Read by the gbpa-bs adapter. 61,722 Freeport address points in `CSV/addresses.csv`, each with block-and-parcel number, street, city and island. Covers the City of Freeport only.
sources.coverage: Freeport address points, `CSV/addresses.csv` of the GitHub repository `GBPA/gis-datafiles` (8,213,284 bytes, sha256 `201658bd153382c1403d9639851b8ef2613573b4a8b9d58436043656cc80a067`, last commit 2018-01-16), retrieved 2026-10-18 with the repository's GeoJSON copy. **Measured 61,722 records**, four with a quoted line break inside `FullStName` (`Santa Maria \r\nSanta Maria Avenue`). Every record names City `Freeport` (15,896 after the adapter) or `Lucaya` (45,789) and Island `Grand Bahama`; the file covers the City of Freeport only. `AddressNum` holds the block-and-parcel number (`8-29`, `UU-3`) and `Address` writes it before the street in all 61,722 records. The `gbpa-bs` adapter writes 61,685 rows.

personalDataReview.because: The fifteen columns were read in full: coordinates, object and address identifiers, parcel and block numbers, the street's prefix, name and suffix, the full address, the house number, city and island. `AltName` is the only free-text name column, populated on 141 rows that the adapter keeps as venues; they name schools, businesses and buildings (`Lucayan International School`). Two hold initials and a surname (`J.S. Johnson`, `G.B. Millwork`), which the adapter refuses (`component:venue:names-a-person`), so no person's name reaches a row.

sources.name: Azərbaycanda obyektlər və məkanlar
sources.authorityBasis: The ministry's Digital Ecology Information System publishes the objects-and-places points the Geodesy and Cartography Agency maintains
sources.access: One GeoJSON on opendata.az, CKAN dataset `azerbaycanda-obyektler-ve-mekanlar`
sources.publisher: Azərbaycan Respublikasının Ekologiya və Təbii Sərvətlər Nazirliyi
sources.note: Read by the opendata-az adapter. 11,807 named places in Baku, Sumgayit and Absheron, 10,035 with a house number and 10,555 with a street.
sources.coverage: `Azərbaycanda obyektlər və məkanlar`, one GeoJSON from opendata.az (5,083,497 bytes, sha256 `d140c7e8b56a250e6c6bc0a3edd1fc2474b56cb7abb2e928d066ecc8b3848bfc`, Last-Modified 2025-08-05), retrieved 2026-10-18. **Measured 11,807 point features**: Baku 9,774, Sumgayit 1,639 and Absheron 394. `STRT_NAME` (an English transliteration) is present on 10,555 and `STRT_ADDR` on 10,035, of which 5,695 read `0` for no number; 92 rows carry the Azerbaijani street spelling `STRT_N_AZ`. `NEW_ADDR` and `Code_OSM` are empty on every row. The `opendata-az` adapter writes 10,300 rows, 87 of them in Azerbaijani spelling.

personalDataReview.because: The sixteen columns were read in full. Apart from the address and place-type columns, `NAME` and `NAME_AZ` hold the place's name: shops, cafes, pharmacies, ATMs, schools, police stations and monuments (`Store`, `Pharmacy`, `Cafe Beyzade`, `Monument Rahimov`). A surname-ending pattern matched three names in the whole file, each a category word beside a name rather than a person. Single given names used as shop names (`Nicat`, `Aynur`) name the business. The adapter refuses names without a three-letter run as codes. No column names an owner, occupant or contact.

sources.name: Address_Point_(Public_View)
sources.authorityBasis: The Bureau of Statistics and Plans GIS publishes Guam's address points on the Government of Guam GISWEB Portal
sources.access: ArcGIS FeatureServer `Address_Point_(Public_View)` layer 0 on services2.arcgis.com, no key
sources.publisher: Government of Guam Bureau of Statistics and Plans
sources.note: Read by the bsp-gu adapter. 34,323 address points with house number, street, unit and village.
sources.coverage: Government of Guam GISWEB Portal `Address_Point_(Public_View)`, FeatureServer layer 0 (item `77d4bfb0fff04c868fe528a1890b4eb0`, modified 2026-05-02), read whole on 2026-10-18 as 18 GeoJSON pages of the layer's 2,000-record maximum (49,746,194 bytes). **Measured 34,323 features** with 34,323 distinct `FID`, matching the layer's own count. Columns include `HOUSE_NUM`, `PRE_DIR`, `STREETNAME`, `STR_TYPE`, `UNIT`, `FullRdNm`, `CITY`, `FullAddres` (`452 RT 10 BARRIGADA GU`) and NG911 fields that are mostly blank; `Post_Code` is blank on every feature. `CITY` names one of Guam's 19 villages, in 47 spellings, and is blank on 4,024. The `bsp-gu` adapter writes 29,889 rows and refuses rows with no street (3,094) or no recognised village (730).

personalDataReview.because: The layer's columns were read in full: an address-point identifier, the house number, directional prefix, street name and type, unit, full road name, village and full address, coordinates, and NG911 fields (postcode, place type, elevation, discrepancy agency) that are blank or coded. No column names an owner, occupant or contact.

sources.name: Liste des bureaux de poste, agences postales et relais poste (laposte-poincont2)
sources.authorityBasis: La Poste, France's universal postal service provider, publishes the list of its own points of contact (Branche Réseau)
sources.access: data-fair dataset `laposte-poincont2` on data.laposte.fr, paged from `/data-fair/api/v1/datasets/laposte-poincont2/lines`, no key
sources.note: Read by the fr-laposte-poincont adapter and the structures layer. 19,858 sites in the 2026-11-14 pull (data updated 2026-11-08): 7,075 agences postales communales, 6,550 bureaux de poste, 4,258 relais poste, 1,725 points partenaires, 236 agences postales intercommunales and 14 others, in metropolitan France, the overseas departments and Andorra, each with a label, a street line, a postcode, a locality, an INSEE commune code and a point.
sources.coverage: `laposte-poincont2` as data.laposte.fr served it on 2026-11-14 (data updated 2026-11-08): 19,858 sites, of which the adapter emits 19,603: FR 19,311, RE 98, GP 68, MQ 55, GF 40, YT 20, MF 7, BL 2, PM 2. Refusals: a street line the French line reader cannot place 211, a complement naming the keeper by an honorific 20, no street line 17, Andorra 7. `complement_d_adresse` is read by no row. The structures layer files the 18,133 sites that aren't `Point partenaire` as post offices.

personalDataReview.because: The list holds post offices, communal postal agencies, relais poste and partner points, and their addresses are facility addresses. Two fields can name a person. `complement_d_adresse` sometimes names a relais keeper (`MME CHAMBARD`) or a shop trading under the keeper's name (`TABAC GUDIN MIREILLE`); the adapter reads it into no row. The site label of a relais or partner point is the shop's trading name, which for a sole trader can hold the keeper's surname (`BRENOD GUDIN BURALISTE`); the label is the name the shop trades under and is read as a venue. The 20 rows whose complement opens with an honorific are refused, and the structures layer files them without their label. A surname in a label whose complement holds no honorific passes, which is the residual exposure.

sources.name: ACNC Registered Charities
sources.authorityBasis: The ACNC, the national charity regulator, publishes the register of charities it maintains
sources.access: CSV resource of the data.gov.au dataset `acnc-register`, updated weekly, no key
sources.note: Read by the au-acnc-register corpus adapter and the evaluation source of the same id, through one reader. 66,623 charities in the 2026-11-14 pull, each with up to three address lines, a town, a state and a postcode; 6,340 carry no address because the ACNC withholds it.
sources.coverage: The register as served on 2026-11-14: 66,623 charities; 6,340 carry no address because the ACNC withholds it; 36,118 single street lines with a house number become address records, in all eight states and territories. The `au-acnc-register` adapter emits 30,843 rows; 5,275 records repeat another charity's address. Refusals besides the withheld: a street line whose number the splitter cannot place 7,288, a post-office box 6,566, several address lines 5,992, no house number 3,372, no ABN 613, no state 184.

personalDataReview.because: The register holds the address each charity gives the ACNC, published under the ACNC Act with an approved withholding route for a charity that asks. A small charity's address can be a responsible person's home, and its legal name can be a person's name (a family trust or foundation). The training rows read only the address, never the name, and no row joins the address to a person, so an address that is a home stands without its occupant. NPPES keeps a sole practitioner's name beside the practice address on HHS's FOIA determination; no such determination covers the ACNC's names, so these rows go further and drop the name on every row. A charity's later withholding request reaches the dataset at its next weekly update, so a refetch drops it.
